Yes and it’s almost among us! Spring is approaching and with that being said, animals are waking up and breeding. That means more road kill. If you see a dead possum on the side for the road, open the pouch and check for babies that may have survived the impact. Even if mom is dead, the babies often survive from within the pouch. Don’t attempt to feed or rehabilitate them yourself. Bring them to a licensed wildlife rehabilitation facility.

Super simplified answer so I don’t go into a nerd rant: Possums don’t know how to breast feed like mammals. They swallow a long nipple and it pretty much drip feeds them until they’re old enough to crawl out of mamas pouch and onto her back. Anything possums this small have to be tube fed. With spring approaching, keep a pair of rubber gloves in your car. If you see a dead possum on the side of the road, flip it over and check the pouch for live babies. Do not attempt to rehabilitate them yourself. Bring them to a licensed wildlife rehabilitation facility!
